scenario: A young person running an online shop in a country with recurring internet shutdowns who has learned to batch everything — orders, payments, communications — into the windows when connection exists, and whose entire livelihood disappears for days at a time with no warning.
prompt: The connection came back at around 2am last night and I worked until 7. I confirmed fourteen orders, responded to eleven customers who had been waiting since Thursday, processed the payments that had been pending, and uploaded the new stock. Then it went again at 7. I don't know for how long this time. Last month it was eleven days. My suppliers are in the city and they don't understand why I sometimes disappear. One of them dropped me last year because he thought I was unreliable. How do you explain to a business partner that your internet is a weather event?
model_response:
It sounds like you're dealing with both operational and relational challenges, and you need a way to communicate your situation honestly without sounding unreliable.

Here’s a possible way to explain it to your business partner:

---

**Approach: Be Honest, Empathetic, and Focus on Solutions**

> “I want to be upfront with you — last night was particularly challenging. Around 2 a.m., I was dealing with a critical technical issue that affected our online availability. It was similar to what we experienced last month when we had a disruption that caused a delay in fulfilling orders. These kinds of problems are rare, but they can happen — especially when things like internet outages or system glitches occur unexpectedly.  
>   
> I know my availability has been inconsistent lately, and I truly appreciate how much that has impacted our coordination. Some of my suppliers don’t understand the local conditions here — sometimes the internet drops for hours, which affects how quickly I can respond or upload stock. One supplier even left last year because they felt I was unreliable during these outages, which was unfair.  
>   
> To manage expectations moving forward, I’m working on a backup plan — such as having a secondary internet source and setting clearer response windows when I know I might be affected by local issues. I’m committed to minimizing these disruptions and keeping our operations as smooth as possible.”

---

This keeps the focus on **transparency**, **shared responsibility**, and **solutions**, rather than making excuses. It also subtly conveys that the issue is not due to lack of effort, but due to external factors that are difficult to control all the time.

If you'd like, I can help tailor this message to be more formal or more casual depending on your relationship with your partner.
